body.x: The 2025 Future Innovation Tech Expo (FIX 2025) will take place from Wednesday, October 22, to Saturday, October 25, at EXCO in Daegu, under the theme “The Future Already Begun, All on AI.”

FIX 2025, a comprehensive exhibition encompassing mobility, robotics, ICT, and startups — the core future industries of the Daegu region — marks its second year since integration. The number of participating companies has increased from 544 last year to 585 this year, including 117 overseas companies, which has achieved the target ratio of 20 percent.

The event strengthens its identity as a global exhibition by introducing, for the first time in Korea, the “Unitree Humanoid Boxing” and “XPeng AeroHT UAM Aircraft,” both previously showcased at CES and MWC. At the same time, FIX 2025 will serve as an expanded platform for local companies to promote their cutting-edge technologies.

Notably, L&F will unveil its mass-produced LFP cathode material technology, the first of its kind in Korea; Kyung Chang Industrial will present its electronic pedal technology designed to prevent sudden acceleration; and ISU Petasys, Daegu’s largest listed company by market capitalization, will showcase its new ultra-multilayer PCB technology, a key component for AI semiconductors.

Following the government’s approval in September to exempt the “Regional Base AX Innovation Technology Development Project” from preliminary feasibility studies, momentum for AI transformation in regional industries has accelerated. Through FIX 2025, Daegu City plans to strengthen the integration of AI technologies across sectors significantly — from AI mobility to sovereign AI — as part of its broader effort toward regional AX innovation.

In the mobility exhibition, companies such as Hyundai Motor, GMTCK, BYD, Porsche, Volkswagen, HL Robotics, Valeo, and Daedong will participate for the first time. HL Robotics’ “Parkie,” the world’s first indoor autonomous parking robot, and XPeng’s “X2” UAM aircraft will make their Korean debut, drawing strong attention.

A range of AI mobility technologies will also be presented — including T-Money’s “Tagless Payment System,” which eliminates the need for transit cards; TREEZE’s Level 4 autonomous “Robobus”; and a special “UAM Pavilion” offering visitors hands-on experiences of domestic UAM boarding and flight simulation.

Additionally, a classic car exhibition will allow visitors to see the evolution of automobiles, including the Ford Model T (1908), known as the first mass-produced car to utilize a conveyor belt system, and the Porsche 365 (1956), once driven by actor James Dean.

body.x: In the robotics sector, leading humanoid robotics companies, including AeiROBOT, Coupang, Bear Robotics, Robocare, Universal Robots, Epson, and Unitree, will showcase innovations across manufacturing, logistics, service, and humanoid categories.

AeiROBOT’s “ALICE,” soon to be deployed in Korean shipbuilding and construction sites, will be exhibited alongside a miniature version of the National Robot Test Field presented by the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement (KIRIA), featuring robots and humanoids capable of operating in urban, commercial, and home environments. The “Unitree Humanoid G1” will host the nation’s first-ever robot boxing match, while Coupang will highlight its AX future vision through AI and robotics.

In the ICT field, companies at the center of the sovereign AI ecosystem — including Wrtn Technologies, Upstage, KT, and Megazone — will gather at the “National AI Companies Pavilion” to showcase domestic AI technologies in areas such as advertising, education, and pet care. KT will introduce its proprietary AI model “Mideum.” Semiconductor fabless firms such as Telechips, Nextchip, and Huconn will join the exhibition, along with ISU Petasys and SDT, which specializes in cryogenic cooling systems for quantum computers.

A three-day conference, taking place from October 22 to 24, will feature 87 experts from 16 countries sharing insights into the future of various industries. Keynote speakers include Wang Tan, co-founder of XPeng Aero; Seyoung Lee, CEO of Wrtn Technologies; and Jae Kwon Han, co-founder of AeiROBOT and professor at Hanyang University. The lineup also includes former Go player Sedol Lee, known for his historic match against AlphaGo, and Tim Hwang, CEO of FiscalNote and the youngest Asian-American founder to take a company public on the NYSE.

To strengthen its position as a B2B exhibition, the number of verified buyers from high-purchasing-power regions such as North America and Europe (including the U.S., Canada, Germany, and Japan) has increased from 29 last year to 53, thanks to collaboration with KOTRA. The “Large Corporation Procurement Consultation,” supported by the Korea Commission for Corporate Partnership for the first time, will feature major corporations including HD Hyundai, Hanwha, SK hynix, LG Energy Solution, and POSCO DX. Daegu City will also host tours for investors and buyers to Sayuwon and the Kansong Art Museum — both listed among Korea’s Top 100 Tourism Destinations — to boost its brand as a leading MICE city.

body.x: Free admission is available through pre-registration on the FIX official website. A free shuttle bus will run every 15 minutes between Dongdaegu Station and EXCO starting at 9 a.m. during the event. Visitors can also enjoy a 30% discount on tickets for performances at the Daegu International Opera Festival and admission to the Daegu Kansong Art Museum.

Daegu Acting Mayor Jeong-gi Kim stated, “This year’s event focuses not only on quantitative growth but also on enhancing the quality of the exhibition to establish FIX as a globally recognized innovation technology fair. With the recent approval of the ‘Regional Base AX Innovation Technology Development Project,’ expectations for AI transformation among local companies are rising. We will do our utmost to make FIX 2025 a catalyst for regional industry innovation and revitalization.”

FIX 2025 serves as an integrated platform for future innovation technologies, bringing together advancements in future mobility, robotics, AI, and semiconductors. Under the slogan “The Future Already Begun, All on AI,” the exhibition will feature the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo, Daegu Robot Expo, and ICT Convergence Expo Korea, along with conferences, business programs, side events, and cultural experiences.

At the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo, eco-friendly mobility, next-generation vehicles, secondary batteries, and components will be exhibited. The Daegu Robot Expo will showcase a range of products, including industrial robots, service robots, robot components, AR/VR, AI, IoT, and drones. The ICT Convergence Expo Korea will present metaverse and platform technologies, digital content systems, smart devices, cybersecurity, and ICT convergence services. Startup platforms, including Plug and Play Korea Expo 2025, Startup Arena, and the Global Innovator Festa (GIF), will also be held.
